identity.title: POCUS lung: subpleural consolidation with air bronchograms / hepatization (+/- focal B-lines) for pneumonia

technique.how: With a 3.5-5 MHz microconvex or curvilinear probe scan anterior, lateral and posterior zones of each hemithorax (at least 8-12 regions), longitudinally across rib spaces. Look for a subpleural hypoechoic tissue-like (hepatized) area with irregular deep border (shred sign), hyperechoic punctate or linear air bronchograms, possibly focal B-lines or a small effusion.
technique.prerequisites: Patient positioned to allow posterior views (sit up or roll); operator trained in lung ultrasound.
technique.contraindications: None absolute; chest wall wounds, dressings or subcutaneous emphysema limit windows.

interpretation.positive_finding: A subpleural consolidation with air bronchograms strongly supports pneumonia (pooled LR+ ~17; single multicentre study LR+ 40). Bilateral diffuse B-lines without consolidation point instead to cardiogenic edema.
interpretation.negative_finding: A normal lung ultrasound makes pneumonia unlikely (pooled LR- 0.07), but about 8% of pneumonic lesions do not reach the pleura and are missed.
interpretation.pitfalls: Atelectasis, contusion, infarction from PE, and tumour can all appear as consolidation; dynamic air bronchograms favour pneumonia over obstructive atelectasis. Deep or central infiltrates not touching the pleura are invisible.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: treat as pneumonia and look for effusion/complications; negative in a low-probability patient: pursue HF, PE or other causes before empiric antibiotics.

estimates.target_condition: Pneumonia (LUS positive = consolidation per included study criteria)
estimates.population: Adults with suspected pneumonia; 10 studies, n=1172 (6 ED/hospital ward, 4 ICU); LUS by highly skilled sonographers in 7 studies
estimates.reference_standard: Chest radiograph and/or chest CT, with or without clinical criteria, per included study
estimates.quote: Pooled sensitivity and specificity for the diagnosis of pneumonia using LUS were 94% (95% CI, 92%-96%) and 96% (94%-97%), respectively
estimates.location: Abstract, Results; full text (PMC4005846) Results 'Overall meta-analysis' and Figure 2

estimates.target_condition: Pneumonia (same pooled analysis as above — likelihood-ratio entry, split only to respect the quote cap)
estimates.population: Adults with suspected pneumonia; 10 studies, n=1172 (6 ED/hospital ward, 4 ICU); LUS by highly skilled sonographers in 7 studies
estimates.reference_standard: Chest radiograph and/or chest CT, with or without clinical criteria, per included study
estimates.quote: pooled positive and negative LRs were 16.8 (7.7-37.0) and 0.07 (0.05-0.10), respectively
estimates.location: Abstract, Results; full text (PMC4005846) Results 'Overall meta-analysis' and Figure 2

estimates.target_condition: Pneumonia (LUS consolidation) — ED and medical ward subgroup
estimates.population: 6 studies of patients admitted to EDs or medical wards with suspected pneumonia
estimates.reference_standard: Chest radiograph and/or chest CT, with or without clinical criteria, per included study
estimates.quote: patients admitted to EDs or medical wards, LUS had a pooled sensitivity of 95% (95% CI, 93% to 97%) and pooled specificity of 94% (95% CI, 91% to 97%)
estimates.location: Full text (PMC4005846), Results, 'Subgroup analysis by patient type and physician training'

estimates.target_condition: Pneumonia (LUS consolidation) — operators were trained ED physicians or general practitioners (non-expert)
estimates.population: 2 studies in which ED physicians or GPs performed LUS after brief training
estimates.reference_standard: Chest radiograph and/or chest CT, with or without clinical criteria, per included study
estimates.quote: used ED physicians or general practitioners (n = 2), LUS had a pooled sensitivity of 93% (95% CI, 85% to 97%) and pooled specificity of 92% (95% CI, 84% to 96%)
estimates.location: Full text (PMC4005846), Results, 'Subgroup analysis by patient type and physician training'

estimates.target_condition: Community-acquired pneumonia (LUS-positive infiltrate; 86.7% showed air bronchogram)
estimates.population: 362 patients with suspected CAP, 14 European centres, prospective; CAP confirmed in 229 (63.3%)
estimates.reference_standard: Chest radiograph in two planes, or low-dose CT when radiograph inconclusive/negative with positive LUS
estimates.quote: LUS revealed a sensitivity of 93.4% (95% CI, 89.2%-96.3%), specificity of 97.7% (95% CI, 93.4%-99.6%)

estimates.target_condition: Community-acquired pneumonia (same Reissig 2012 cohort — likelihood-ratio entry, split only to respect the quote cap)
estimates.population: 362 patients with suspected CAP, 14 European centres, prospective; CAP confirmed in 229 (63.3%)
estimates.reference_standard: Chest radiograph in two planes, or low-dose CT when radiograph inconclusive/negative with positive LUS
estimates.quote: likelihood ratios (LRs) of 40.5 (95% CI, 13.2-123.9) for positive and 0.07 (95% CI, 0.04-0.11) for negative results

sources.citation: Chavez MA, Shams N, Ellington LE, Naithani N, Gilman RH, Steinhoff MC, Santosham M, Black RE, et al. Lung ultrasound for the diagnosis of pneumonia in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Respir Res. 2014.

Reissig A, Copetti R, Mathis G, Mempel C, Schuler A, Zechner P, Aliberti S, Neumann R, et al. Lung ultrasound in the diagnosis and follow-up of community-acquired pneumonia: a prospective, multicenter, diagnostic accuracy study. Chest. 2012.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative scan to withhold antibiotics in a septic or immunocompromised patient with high pretest probability; central infiltrates are missed.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Consolidation with large effusion, hypoxia or hemodynamic instability warrants urgent imaging and sepsis management; consider empyema or necrotizing pneumonia.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Meta-analysis notes most studies used self-reported expert sonographers; ED/GP-operator subgroup performed slightly worse (sens 93%, spec 92%). No kappa reported in the abstract.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Operator trained in lung ultrasound (studies used experts with >=100 exams or >10 years, or ED physicians after ~6 hours of training); systematic multi-zone protocol including posterior chest.

extraction_notes: Pooled estimate from the abstract and PMC open-access full text of Chavez 2014; sens/spec and LR rows are split into paired entries (same analysis) because one verbatim quote holding all four numbers with CIs exceeds the quote cap; the same applies to the Reissig 2012 rows. Positive LUS criterion in 9/10 included studies was 'consolidation' (Table 3 of full text); one study used 'alveolar and interstitial' findings, so the title's air-bronchogram/hepatization definition is close but not identical. Reissig 2012 is the largest prospective primary study (cited as source 1); its abstract also reports '86.7% (183 of 211) an air bronchogram' and '97.6% (205 of 211) of patients with CAP showed breath-dependent motion of infiltrates' (Abstract, Results). Reissig full text was not retrievable via PMC. Chavez abstract: AUC 0.99 (0.98-0.99); ICU subgroup (4 studies) sens 93% (89-95), spec 97% (95-98) (full text, subgroup paragraph) not entered as a separate estimate to limit duplication.
